title: H 4919 (124th General Assembly): Absentee voting
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) 7-15-385(E) (absentee return only; no provisional-ballot, cure, affidavit or free-ID remedy is stated)
(quote) An election official must not accept a return-addressed envelope until the provisions of this section have been met.
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) 7-15-385(D)(1) (photo ID shown when the sealed absentee envelope is delivered in person)
(quote) When an applicant, or an applicant's authorized immediate family member or authorized representative, presents himself to deliver a return-addressed envelope pursuant to this section, he must produce a valid and current: (a) driver's license issued by a state within the United States; (b) another form of identification containing a photograph issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles or its equivalent by a state within the United States; (c) passport; (d) military identification containing a photograph issued by the federal government; or (e) South Carolina voter registration card containing a photograph of the voter.
(section) 7-15-385(D)(2)
(quote) An election official must verify that the name and photograph on the identification is the applicant, or the applicant's authorized immediate family member or authorized representative, as applicable.
(section) 7-15-330(B)(2) (identifying number, not a photo ID, to request the absentee application)
(quote) A person who makes a request for an application to vote by absentee ballot, either for himself or on behalf of another elector as permitted by this section, must provide the following: (a) for the elector for whom the request is being made, the elector's: (i) name; (ii) date of birth; and (iii) last four digits of his social security number;
(d_proof_of_citizenship)
(section) 7-3-70(c), added by SECTION 32 (database report; no voter is asked for proof of citizenship)
(quote) The Department of Motor Vehicles must furnish the executive director a monthly report of all non-United States citizens who are issued a driver's license or identification card. All reports must contain the name of the driver or identification cardholder, social security number, if any, and date of birth.
(section) 7-5-340(A)(1) lead-in
(quote) ensure that the name of a qualified elector is removed from the official list of eligible voters within seven days of receipt of information confirming:
(section) 7-5-340(A)(1)(d), added
(quote) the elector is not a citizen of the United States;
(e_other_rule)
(section) 7-5-170(2) (added to the registration oath)
(quote) and that, to my knowledge, I am neither registered nor intend to register to vote in another state or county
(section) 7-5-186(A)
(quote) The executive director must conduct an annual general registration list maintenance program to maintain accurate voter registration records in the statewide voter registration system.
(section) 7-15-430(B) (provisional ballot for a voter issued an absentee ballot who has not returned it)
(quote) The provisional ballot must only be counted if the absentee ballot is not received by the time for the closing of the polls on election day
(other) 7-13-25 (SECTION 1): creates early in-person voting, at 1 to 7 county early voting centers over the two weeks before every election; hours set by election type; no ID rule is attached to early voting.
(other) 7-11-10 and 7-13-320(D): a candidate may not file more than one statement of candidacy for one office, may not be nominated by more than one party for one office, and may not appear on a ballot twice.
(other) 7-15-220, 7-15-380: absentee-ballot witness must be 18 or older and the witness's printed name is added to the oath (in addition to signature and address).
(other) 7-15-320: rewrites the list of reasons for voting absentee; adds an 'unable to vote during early voting and election day' category and removes vacation, attending sick persons and funeral reasons.
(other) 7-15-330: who may request an absentee application (voter, immediate family, authorized representative), limit of five requests per person besides himself, a record of requestor and elector data, and applications due by the eleventh day before the election.
(other) 7-15-385: absentee envelope may be returned only by mail to the main county office, in person at the county office or an early voting center, or by a family member or authorized representative; a person may not return more than five envelopes besides his own (felony penalty).
(other) 7-15-420, 7-13-35: absentee envelopes may be examined from 7:00 a.m. two days before election day; tabulation may begin 7:00 a.m. on election day; public reporting of absentee results before polls close is a felony.
(other) 7-15-430: absentee voters who have not returned the ballot may vote a provisional ballot in person or at an early voting center.
(other) 7-5-170: voter registration applications are date-stamped; oath adds not registered or intending to register in another state or county.
(other) 7-13-320, 7-13-610, 7-13-1330, 7-13-1340, 7-13-1620, 7-13-1640, 7-13-440 (repealed): ballot authentication features; voting-system procurement, ballot images, record retention (24 months), disabling of network connections, certification rules.
(other) 7-3-40, 7-5-186, 7-5-330, 7-5-340, 7-3-45, 7-5-350: death and incapacity reports (including out-of-state deaths), annual list maintenance, notice to voters on data discrepancies, faster removals, annual report to the General Assembly.
(other) 7-25-30 and election-offence sections (7-25-20, 7-25-110, 7-25-120, 7-25-160, 7-25-170, 7-25-65, 7-25-180): State Law Enforcement Division reporting hotline, higher penalties, ban on paying for absentee ballots, campaign material ban widened to 500 feet and the early voting period.
(other) 7-1-110: the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House may intervene and have standing in election-law challenges.
(other) 7-3-10, 7-3-20, 7-3-25, 7-5-50, 7-5-190: State Election Commission members and executive director appointment, qualifications and removal; standardized county processes; ban on private gifts; security standards. (The Senate rewrite also adds a voter education program.)
(other) 7-15-470 repealed: ends in-person absentee voting.
(other) SECTION 45: most sections take effect on approval by the Governor; SECTION 2 on January 1, 2023; SECTIONS 3 and 6 on July 1, 2022.
(other) version: 2022-02-03_Introduced: slot c only. 7-15-340 adds a requirement that an absentee application contain the voter's 'South Carolina driver's license number or other personal or unique identification number associated with a valid and current, government-issued photo identification referenced in Section 7-13-710(A)' (cross-reference to the 2011 photo-ID list; the list is not reprinted). 7-15-385 adds that a person authorized to return another voter's absentee envelope must show one of five photo IDs (SC driver's license, other DMV photo ID, passport, military photo ID, SC voter registration card with photo), recorded on the authorization form. No slots a, b or d. Does not otherwise touch 7-13-710.
(other) version: 2022-02-23_Comm-Sub (House Judiciary): the application ID-number rule is replaced by 'the last four digits of the voter's social security number' (7-15-340(B)(2)); 7-15-385 returnee photo-ID text unchanged. Bill grows from about 24k to 84k characters with many election-administration sections. Text file also reprints the introduced bill after the committee text.
(other) version: 2022-02-24_Comm-Sub: same as 02-23 apart from a typographic fix; ID text unchanged.
(other) version: 2022-03-02_Amended (as passed by the House): same ID text as the committee version (last four of social security number on the application; returnee photo ID). Floor changes compared with 02-24: early-voting wording, a candidate-statement wording fix, and a new 7-3-20(C) audit item; none touch ID or citizenship.
(other) version: 2022-03-03_Amended: same as 03-02 apart from a typographic fix; ID text unchanged.
(other) version: 2022-03-10_Amended: same as 03-03 apart from a one-word fix ('One' to 'Once'); ID text unchanged.
(other) version: 2022-04-12_Amended (House text as printed in the Senate when recalled from committee): same operative text as 03-10; ID text unchanged.
(other) version: 2022-04-20_Amended (Senate amended, second reading): rewrites 7-15-330 so any request for an absentee application must give the elector's name, date of birth and last four social security digits; deletes the 7-15-340 section; 7-15-385 now requires photo ID from the applicant too when delivering in person (the five forms now say 'driver's license issued by a state within the United States' and 'Department of Motor Vehicles or its equivalent by a state within the United States'; the voter registration card reference to 7-5-675 is dropped); adds 7-15-385(E) refusal to accept the envelope until met; adds citizenship text for the first time (7-5-340(A)(1)(d) removal of non-citizens; 7-3-70(c) DMV monthly report of non-citizens); adds many other sections.
(other) version: 2022-04-21_Amended ('As passed by the Senate'): ID and citizenship text unchanged from 04-20; small wording fixes (drops 'at a minimum' from 7-15-330(B)(2); 7-15-430 provisional-ballot wording).
(other) version: 2022-04-22_Amended: same as 04-21 apart from punctuation fixes; ID and citizenship text unchanged.
(other) version: 2022-04-26_Amended (furthest version, Senate-passed text after the bill was committed in the House on 4/26): ID and citizenship text unchanged; only early-voting hours in 7-13-25(F) differ from 04-22. Quotes above are from this version.
(other) note: H 4919 never became law: it passed the House 3/2/2022 (114-0) and the Senate 4/21 (43-0) with amendments, was committed to House Judiciary on 4/26, and the Senate-passed text became the House-amended S 108 instead (Act 150 of 2022, see SC-S-108-2022). The bill does not amend 7-13-710 (in-person photo ID), so slot a is 'not stated'; the only reference to 7-13-710 is in the introduced version's application rule and it is a cross-reference, not a reprint. Photo ID applies only when someone delivers a sealed absentee envelope in person; mail returns need no ID. In the introduced version the ID-number requirement was on the absentee application; from the committee version on it is the last four social security digits instead. Citizenship: no voter proof; the DMV non-citizen report and removal of non-citizens appear only from 4/20/2022. Markup: the files mark new and struck words from existing law; Senate and House floor amendments are not separately marked, so what each adopted floor amendment did is inferred only by comparing versions. Quotes join list items into one line.
